ESE Presentation

Meeting recordings preserve proposals, explanations and decisions, but finding the relevant passage means manually scrubbing through audio.
Speech-recognition errors change the words an extractor sees; speaker-attribution errors credit a contribution to the wrong person.
A useful review tool therefore needs an explicit evaluation target and a trace back to the original recording.
Noisy inputs
ASR word errors and diarization errors propagate into every downstream label.
Discussion ≠ decision
A passage can concern a decision without recording a final agreement or action.
Multilingual meetings
Hindi and Hinglish speech must be handled honestly by an English-trained detector.
Meeting assistants, Whisper, diarization, multilingual benchmarks

Work | Focus | Relevance to InfluenceIQ
Tur et al. 2010 — CALO | Transcription + semantic interpretation | Broader assistant; we bound the task to discussion review
Radford et al. 2023 — Whisper | Multilingual ASR, weak supervision | Basis of the local faster-whisper recogniser
Bain et al. 2023 — WhisperX | Time-accurate long-form ASR | Motivates alignment; full pipeline not used
Bredin 2023; Plaquet & Bredin 2023 | pyannote diarization; overlap-aware powerset | Report speaker attribution separately
Macháček et al. 2023 | Streaming Whisper commit policies | We use bounded preview windows + full post-capture pass
DISPLACE 2023/24; Vistaar 2023 | Multilingual diarization; Indian-language ASR | Motivate code-switched meeting evaluation
MeetingBank 2023; ExplainMeetSum 2023 | Meeting summarisation; evidence-aligned summaries | We give extractive, source-linked suggestions instead
Weak traceability
Generated summaries rarely link each claim back to the exact segment, speaker and timestamp.
Cloud dependence
Most meeting assistants rely on remote inference, which conflicts with local, private review.
Non-comparable scores
Published summarisation and diarization scores are not baselines for binary discussion membership.
Hidden error propagation
ASR and diarization errors are seldom reported separately, and Hindi–English meetings are under-evaluated.

Recognition is cached separately from speaker attribution, so speaker fixes reuse saved words.
Scores are ranking signals, not calibrated probabilities.

Calibrating the threshold to 0.9 on development excerpts cuts fragmentation; speech-region detection barely changes.

InfluenceIQ delivers offline meeting processing with source-linked discussion suggestions and human review.
The development-selected forest/linear mix reaches 53.54% historical F1 on oracle transcripts, with precision and ranking trade-offs.
Turbo ASR gives large Hindi gains but regresses on historical English, so model choice stays explicit.
Negative trials, provenance and missing downstream metrics remain visible.
